sentences.text: Shri Sanjeev Kumar Rawat learned counsel for the petiti  Shri Bhaskar Agrawal learned counsel for the respondent The petitioners have challenged the legality and validity of the notification dated 29.09.2014 published in the Gazette on 03.10.2014, which has been issued in exercise of the powers conferred by column No.3 of serial No.2 of the First Schedule read with sub-Section (2) of Section 30 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred as "Act, 2013"), whereby the State Government has notified that in cases of rural areas, the factor by which the market value is to be multiplied shall be 1.00 (One).

Counsel for the petitioner argued that the fixing of the multiplicity of "One" for the market value is contrary to the provision of Section 107 of the Act, 2013, which provides that the State Legislature can fix the compensation more than the compensation provided under the Act.

He further argued that since it is a beneficial legislation, the same cannot be restricted to "One" as initially it was provided for the rural areas with multiple factor from "One" to "Two" depending on the distance of the village from urban areas.
Considering the said submission, issue notice to the respondents on payment of PF within seven working days by Registered AD mode.
2 WP-5177-2026 Notices be made returnable within six weeks.
List the matter after six weeks alongwith Writ Petition Nos.39399/2025 and 29999/2023 and 10465/2024.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) 
 JUDGE   Sourabh Pallav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85220619/
